text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London edged higher in late afternoon trade, with front month August closing steady, while other positions finished lower. August closed at an unchanged $319.10 a tonne and total turnover was 5,532 lots, which was boosted by switches and AAs.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed a thinly traded session firmer amid steady trade buying, trade sources said. The buying offset early speculative selling which pressured the benchmark October contract to its downside target of 11.00 cents/lb. Speculators slowed their selling and allowed the front month to climb to the day's high of 11.12 cents/lb.

Dealers said the positive close would attract follow-through buying on Thursday, and pegged resistance at the recent high of 11.22 cents/lb in October. The most-active October contract ended 0.05 cents/lb higher at 11.11 cents/lb, while second position March closed up 0.04 cents/lb at 11.25 cents/lb. The rest of the board finished 0.04 to 0.08 cents/lb firmer.

EUROPEAN UNION - EU beet sugar output is expected to fall to 16.05 million tonnes, white value, in 1997/98 (July/June) from 16.51 million last season, the European Commission said. Taking account of a prospective cane sugar production of 270,000 tonnes and 44,000 tonnes derived from molasses desugaring total EU output is to reach 16.37 million tonnes compared to 16.84 million in 1996/97.

The area sown to beet in 1997/98 was estimated at 2.043 million ha, up from 2.020 million ha in 1996/97. White sugar yield is likely to drop to 7.86 tonnes per ha, down from 8.18 tonnes the previous year, the Commission said.

EU C-sugar exports in 1997/98 are forecast to drop sharply to 1.95 million tonnes, down from 2.44 million tonnes in 1996/97, while the carry over of C sugar into 1998/99 is expected to rise to 1 million tonnes, up from 917,000 tonnes last year.

UKRAINE - Ukraine has forecast a sugar beet crop of 30 to 31 million tonnes in 1997, up from 24 million tonnes in 1996, Deputy Economy Minister Valentyn Poshyvailo recently said. The area sown to beet reached 1.1 million ha, down from 1.3 million ha the previous year. Beet yields were 3.0 tonnes per ha at the start of July, compared to 2.8 tonnes at the same time the previous year.

Commenting on the higher production forecast, which compares to earlier estimates of 24 million tonnes, Poshyvailo said more favourable weather conditions had set in compared to last year, when a drought at the beginning of the growing season damaged plants.
Given an average beet yield of 21.5 tonnes per ha in the years 1991/92 to 1995/96 it seems as if the projected rise to 27.7 tonnes per ha in 1997/98 may be on the high side.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in April 1997 amounted to 91,681 tonnes, raw value, down from 120,295 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 731,445 tonnes, down from 802,258 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.380 million tonnes against 1.635 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Mauritius with 293,932 tonnes raws against 365,503 tonnes, Guyana with 129,573 tonnes compared to 95,356 tonnes and Brazil with 79,900 tonnes, down from 85,180 tonnes.

Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 59,736 tonnes compared to 48,874 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/April 1996/97 up to 216,869 tonnes against 222,290 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 390,747 tonnes, down from 560,076 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in October/April 1996/97 were Israel with 74,249 tonnes whites against 63,736 tonnes, Norway with 21,650 tonnes against 28,484 tonnes and Italy with 14,732 tonnes, down from 19,073 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 69,000 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 41.846 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on July 7. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to July 2 reached 2,417,825 tonnes, which compares to 2,503,698 tonnes last year.
